title: Silas and the Summer
premise: Orsen Fairweather has spent a decade keeping her heart on a strict training regimen: no attachments beyond her daughter, no risks beyond the bookshop's ledgers. When a freak June snowstorm traps her in the shop overnight with Silas Wren — the charming rival bookseller whose family chain nearly bankrupted her, and the man she loved and lost at twenty-three — old wounds and older want resurface. As the summer unfolds, Silas returns to town to close his family's failing store next door, forcing Orsen to choose between protecting her daughter, her shop, and the carefully contained heart she swore would never be spent again. She finally risks all of it, only to learn Silas is leaving for good; in the last chapter she lets him go rather than ask him to stay — until he chooses to come back, not as a rescue but as a neighbor, and they build something that costs them both and belongs to neither.
about_author: Mara Nakamura is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who now writes love stories about people who read too much and risk too little. She lives by the sea with her partner, two cats, and an ever-growing tower of unsold paperbacks.

chapters.title: The Heart Is a Muscle
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A morning inventory of the bookshop doubles as an inventory of Orsen's rules: measure everything, want nothing. Her daughter Juniper teases her about never dating. Emotional beat: controlled contentment with hairline cracks showing.

chapters.title: The Man Next Door
chapters.summary: Orsen spots movers unloading into the vacant storefront beside hers — Wren & Sons Books, the chain that nearly ruined her. Silas steps out of the truck, unchanged and impossible. POV Orsen. Beat: cold shock dressed as politeness.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He explains he's here to wind down his father's failing branch, not to compete. Orsen doesn't believe him. They agree to a wary truce over bad coffee. Beat: grudging respect flickering under old resentment.

chapters.title: Juniper's Library Card
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Juniper befriends Silas in the shop while Orsen pretends not to watch, and Orsen realizes her daughter is already charmed. Guilt surfaces about the secrets of their shared past. Beat: tenderness complicated by fear.

chapters.title: What Happened in the Snow
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, dual POV. Ten years ago: a snowstorm, a borrowed cabin, the best mistake of their twenties — one night before Silas left without saying goodbye. Beat: aching nostalgia reframed as betrayal.

chapters.title: Inventory Day
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A delivery mix-up forces Orsen and Silas to work side by side shelving stock, trading barbs that keep slipping into laughter. An almost-touch at the same shelf. Beat: attraction reasserting itself against her will.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He finds his father's real accounts: the branch isn't just closing, it's drowning, and his father expects him to strip it for parts. He hides this from Orsen. Beat: dread and the first taste of complicity.

chapters.title: Summer Reading Night
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The shops co-host a children's reading event; Silas performs voices and wins the whole street over. Orsen watches him with Juniper and feels her containment plan failing. Beat: warmth she can't file away.

chapters.title: Pieces, Not the Whole
chapters.summary: A late-night argument becomes a confession: Orsen admits she lends pieces of herself but never the whole. Silas says he'd rather have nothing than pieces. POV alternates. Beat: raw honesty, doors opening and slamming.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. His father offers him a promotion in the city if he closes the branch fast and quietly — which means gutting the block Orsen depends on. Silas stalls. Beat: duty tightening like a fist.

chapters.title: Rain on the Awning
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A summer storm strands them under the shared awning; they talk about the snowstorm night for the first time soberly, each learning what the other actually believed back then. Beat: grief revised into understanding.

chapters.title: Juniper Asks a Question
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Juniper asks why Silas looks at her mother 'like the sad parts of books.' Orsen deflects badly and lies awake cataloguing everything she stands to lose. Beat: maternal fear sharpening into self-awareness.

chapters.title: Compromise
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas secretly begins restructuring the branch as an independent buyout instead of a closure, risking his father's wrath. He asks Orsen, hypothetically, whether second chances exist. Beat: hope disguised as negotiation.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen decides to risk it: she tells Silas she wants the whole thing, no pieces, no exits. They spend the night together, ten years late. Beat: surrender, joy, terror.

chapters.title: Paper Cuts
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The affair goes public on the street; loyal customers take sides, and Orsen's landlord hints the Wren name endangers her lease. Old wounds reopen on new terms. Beat: love colliding with community.

chapters.title: Father's Letter
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. His father discovers the buyout plan, disowns the idea and threatens to sell the building out from under everyone — including Orsen's shop. Silas must choose between inheritance and integrity. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Running Out of Summer
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen learns Silas's city promotion deadline is the end of August — he never mentioned leaving. Feeling like the mistake of his twenties all over again, she withdraws. Beat: betrayal echoing history.

chapters.title: Empty Shelves
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas packs up the branch alone, refusing the promotion, and writes letters he can't send. Orsen won't answer his calls. Beat: rock bottom, chosen sacrifice unrecognized.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The building goes to auction; Orsen scrapes together everything to bid and loses to an anonymous buyer. Devastated, she assumes the worst of Silas. Beat: despair at its lowest point.

chapters.title: Signed, S.W.
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. The anonymous buyer is revealed: Silas bought the building with his inheritance and signed the ground floor over to Orsen's shop at fair rent. She confronts him — furious, then undone — and asks him to stay not as charity but as choice. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. September arrives; the wall between the shops comes down for a shared doorway. Juniper paints the sign. Orsen reflects on hearts as muscles that grow by use, not containment. Beat: quiet, earned happiness.

chapters.title: Silas and the Summer
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating short passages from both POVs across the following year's seasons. The merged shop thrives, his father sends a cautious olive branch, and Orsen finally stops counting what things cost. Final beat: belonging as a daily practice, not a prize.
